controlled_change: One native off/on source-copy producer. Only individual one-row experts in four-token target decode use linear_into at their original contribution offset. Same Q4/Q8 kernels, weights, final reduction, 1460 target slots, 32 draft slots, lazy ngram initialization and reserved bytes. Expert scratch remains off in both arms.
correctness: 42 focused MTP tests pass. Real Q4 fixture validates all destination rows, untouched sentinels, mixed rows, invalid destinations, reversed reads, eviction, all hits, delayed GPU callbacks, cancellation and read/encoding failure drains with all buffers released. Full-model rejection pair and all ordinary pairs match exact logits, tokens, target/draft state and cache behavior. All longer target outputs also match completed historical serial results numerically. Every fresh process has clean host/memory.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Lower verifier and complete cycle latency under the unchanged 12GiB budget; at least 2% short-screen improvement before testing three longer coding cases.
hypothesis: Existing direct output bindings for single-row experts in four-token verification can remove scatter dispatches and improve real MTP requests without changing arithmetic.
limitations: Rejection concerns advancement toward the 5-token/s release target, not correctness or proof of no benefit.
Two short pairs and one pair per longer coding case do not provide a confidence-bounded broad performance claim.
Short prompts are 72/198/93 tokens; no 2K/4K/7K or sustained-session qualification.
App expert-read bytes are not observed device traffic.
Historical serial results are used only for numerical agreement; original unfinished-stage statuses remain unchanged.
Production is unchanged and earlier scratch/packed-Q4 experiments remain separate.
outcome: Both alternating short pairs pass: candidate 5.0408/5.0394 versus control 4.8390/4.9254 tokens/s, geometric-mean latency reduction 3.1374%. Exactly 3110 scatters and 6220 allocations removed. Longer 128-token pairs: merge 4.4128 to 4.4042 (+0.1967% latency), LRU 3.0916 to 3.1595 (-2.1492%), retry 3.6269 to 3.7164 (-2.4102%). Across-case latency reduction 1.4612%, not a repeated-pair confidence bound. Peak footprint 9.7273GiB; expert reads remain 627.91/762.11/718.90MiB per committed token. All longer candidates miss 5 tokens/s.
smallest_experiment: Do not extend this unchanged candidate to 256-token, long-context or release qualification. Retain its exact implementation and small measured gains. The next intervention must address verifier/recovery work and expert reads per committed token; evaluate those dependency costs before another isolated dispatch or allocation change.
